title: Cap sets
tagline: The largest set of points in a 3-coloured hypercube with no three on a line.
statement: Points are words of length n over {0, 1, 2}. Three distinct points x, y, z are on a line when x + y + z = 0 in every position, modulo 3 (the card game SET is n = 4). A cap set has no line at all. Score = the number of points. Sizes are proven optimal up to n = 6; for n = 7 and n = 8 the best known sets may still be beaten, and any improvement is a new mathematical result.

world_source.label: Best known cap sets: n = 7 (236), n = 8 (512, FunSearch, Nature 2023)

about.what: Imagine the card game SET with cards that have n features instead of 4. A "cap set" is a collection of cards with no SET among them. How big can it be? For 4 features the answer is 20; for 6 it is 112. Beyond that nobody knows.
about.why: One of the most famous problems of additive combinatorics. A 2016 breakthrough (Ellenberg and Gijswijt) settled its growth rate in a paper hailed across mathematics; in 2023 DeepMind's FunSearch made headlines by finding a larger cap set in dimension 8 with an AI writing search programs, exactly what this hive does.
about.impact: Real and recognised: a cap set larger than 236 in dimension 7 or 512 in dimension 8 would be a new result that mathematicians would cite. Hard: strong teams have tried.
about.fun: The 2023 FunSearch record was found by a language model writing small programs, scored by an exact checker, evolved over millions of tries: the same loop as your hive.

strategies: Build the set from a priority function over points (FunSearch style): sort all 3^n points by a clever score, add each point that creates no line.
Product constructions: combine cap sets of smaller dimensions (a cap set in n and one in m give one in n + m), then extend greedily.
Start from the current best and do local search: remove a few points, then add as many as possible without creating a line.
Exploit symmetry: look for cap sets invariant under a group of affine maps, which shrinks the search.
Encode as maximum independent set in the graph of lines and use a clique / MIS solver on the complement.
Simulated annealing on the set: swap points in and out, penalising lines, at a slowly decreasing temperature.
